accepted.place: A colliery village's sea parade on delivery morning: one unbroken terrace of small businesses down the near side, the pit gates and winding gear closing the landward head of the road, the five-storey hotel closing the seaward end with the beach and railing beyond it, delivery lorries nosed into the kerb with their tailgates down and crates stacked out on the flags at every doorway.
accepted.activity: Everyone is taking in the morning delivery — lifting crates down off the lorries at the kerb, wheeling sack-trucks in through the doorways, signing the docket on the driver's board, and carrying the empties back out to be loaded up again.
accepted.anchor_structure: The unbroken run of shopfront fascias with the kerb and gutter line beneath them, running from the lower left of the frame up to the pit gates at the top right, splitting the picture into pavement, roadway, shopfronts and the upper windows above them.
accepted.pun_explanation: A neurotransmitter is a chemical messenger and MESSENGER ROW is an ordinary hand-lettered street nameplate that carries one morpheme of the plain-English referent without printing the medical word — the p272 device, inside the Lithium Lift precedent — and the parade is the only mundane container that holds a pit, a hotel, a dairy, a club door, a weaving workshop, a newsagent and a police box at one light source; the delivery round then supplies the mechanism free, because release is a crate carried in off the lorry and reuptake is the same hand carrying the empties back out to be loaded, and each premises signs for its own crate so every messenger stays addressable at its own doorway.

accepted.activity: Everyone is getting a baby weighed and the figure written in the book — undressing one on the mat, holding one over the pan scale, waiting on the mats with the red book open, queueing at the trestle.
accepted.anchor_structure: The run of crash mats and low gym benches laid end to end down the hall, with the stack of folded spare mats standing at its head, carrying from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and splitting the room into porch and buggy park, mat floor, weighing trestle and the boarded-off end under the high windows.
accepted.pun_explanation: CRAWLING and CRUISING are the two motor milestones of the first two years and both are ordinary English words, so a group banner hand-painted CRAWL & CRUISE reads as the perfectly normal name toddler groups genuinely trade under while printing no part of the topic — the p272 device — and the weighing session was chosen over a play barn because it puts every figure in the frame at the same ordinary task with a baby in front of them, gives the numbers a carrier whose real job is bearing digits (pan scale, brass weights, centile crosses, ages in months), and keeps the hall free of climbing frames and steps so that the chapter's one required ladder is the only ladder in the picture.

accepted.place: A tool and plant hire depot on a Saturday morning: a counter with a docket pad and a spike at the front, double-height racking of breakers, mixers and generators down one side, a wash-off bay with a hose reel and a mud grate, a service bench under the window, and the roller shutter half up onto the loading yard. The training room off the counter has its door hooked open, let by the hour as it is every Saturday.
accepted.activity: Everybody is taking a tool out or bringing one back - carrying a breaker to the counter, filling in a docket, hosing mud off a mixer in the wash-off bay, wringing and wiping their hands on a rag at the hand-cleaner drum.
accepted.anchor_structure: The double-height steel racking run of breakers, mixers and generators, running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and splitting the depot into the hire counter, the racking run, the wash-off bay and the open shutter onto the yard.
accepted.pun_explanation: RETT-A-TOOL is the rent-a-X wrap said aloud - one eponym morpheme inside an entirely ordinary hire-trade fascia, the licence Lithium Lift already has, and the diagnosis is never printed. The trade was chosen because this is a hand chapter and a hire depot is a hand business. Staff wring and wipe their hands on rags at the hand-cleaner drum all shift, so the hallmark hand movement is the depot's own paid work rather than a symbol of it. The returns bench holds tools that have come back with their grips and handles stripped off, so purposeful hand use is the thing the depot has lost. The board of hole saws hung in ascending diameters with the largest three pegs empty is a native size chart, which carries head-circumference deceleration with no painted numeral competing against anything. Prader-Willi comes off the staffroom end of the counter: the padlocked consumables cabinet and the chained vending machine are the real management fact, and the slack drive belt on its hook is hypotonia. 22q11 rides the small print, because the excess and damage-waiver catch in the framed hire agreement is the cliche of the trade and CATCH-22 is its own name for itself, while the lime pallet by the mixer bay with its stock card chalked LOW carries the calcium in the trade's own material. The Saturday training room is let by the hour, which is how the classroom stands in this frame as itself. No bay numbers are painted anywhere, so the chromosome number lives on a docket and cannot collide with the sorting depot.

accepted.place: A herb drying loft over the shop on a warm afternoon: tiers of slatted trays on their runners down the length of the floor, bunches hanging from the tie-beam above them, a sorting board and the stove with its damper at the far end, and the packing bench with jars, tins and paper sacks under the window. The family's school-age children work the low tiers after school alongside the adults, satchels dumped on the hooks by the loft stair.

accepted.anchor_structure: The tiered drying rack - the run of slatted trays on their runners with the hanging bunches on the tie-beam above it - crossing the loft from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and dividing it into the tipping floor, the rack run, the sorting board and the packing bench at the window.
accepted.pun_explanation: Dysthymia gives THYME, thyme is said time, and Thyme & Again is a name a herb loft would really trade under. It also says time and again, which is the one thing the chapter's three disorders share: the same low mood, sorted only by its temporal shape. Persistent depressive disorder sits on the stock dates, because whole leaf keeps two years and rubbed leaf keeps one, and the trade stamps both on the lid - the adult threshold and the child threshold printed by a trade that has to print them anyway. DMDD is the children. They work the low tiers alongside the adults, one tray has gone over and the leaf is scattered down the boards, and the spoilage board ruled into a year of weekly columns is chalked 3 against this week. Between times they are sour at the trays, which is the criterion the outburst count is usually taught without. PMDD is the year planner on the post: a column a day, the last four days of every month ruled off and hatched, month after month, kept prospectively for the loft's own reasons. The mimic check is the thermometer and hygrometer, read and chalked daily like everything else in here.

accepted.place: A safety equipment inspection depot on a weekday morning: a receiving bench at the front where kit comes in on its due date, a proof-load gantry with a load cell and a big figured dial, a detector test bench with a gas manifold and alarms sounding along it, a tagging bench with a roll of dated service tags, a back wall of dated boxes, and the shop window onto the kerb.
accepted.activity: Everybody is putting a piece of kit through its due test and tagging it - hanging a harness on the gantry and watching the dial, gassing a detector until it screams, weighing an extinguisher, writing a date on a tag and wiring it on.
accepted.anchor_structure: The instrumented test run - the proof-load gantry with its load cell and figured dial carried on into the detector bench with its manifold and sounding alarms - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the depot into the receiving bench, the test run, the tagging bench and the back wall of dated boxes.
accepted.pun_explanation: GADD carries the acronym inside an ordinary family surname on an ordinary trade fascia, the Ben's Diner device, and nothing on the sign names the disorder. The premises are an inspection and issue depot rather than a kit shop: things arrive on their due date, go through a test and go back out with a dated tag on them, so the visual mass is instruments and paperwork, not racks of wearable stock. That trade is the chapter's core feature made literal. Worry spread across unrelated domains is one hazard to a line on the depot's own wall list - gas, height, fire, noise, eyes - so every domain hands over a separate prop with nothing invented. The paperwork is the numbers layer: the accident-free tally board is a chalked count of days and is the only carrier in the syllabus whose native unit is more days than not, every tag in the trade bears a due date and a six-month interval, and the inspection card is ruled into seven numbered check lines. The gantry and the detector bench give restlessness, muscle tension and startle as people literally under load and literally jumping when an alarm goes off. The almond-shaped personal panic alarms are ordinary stock in this trade, not a substitute for the token. And because the depot fronts onto a street, the bus stop stands where a bus stop stands, in view of the issue hatch.

accepted.place: A paintings conservation studio on an ordinary working weekday: a rank of easels under a slotted raking-light rail, most of them holding Victorian and Edwardian portraits of children with numbered condition tickets tied to their stretchers, and the x-ray viewing box glowing on the end wall. A floor-to-ceiling run of sliding mesh racks stands along the far wall with half of them pulled out on their runners, a drum thermohygrograph ticks above the intake counter at the street door, and the far bay of the racks is under dust sheets.

accepted.pun_explanation: WARD and CRADLE are both genuine terms of this trade - a work is held in the studio's ward, and a cradle is the lattice of battens glued to the back of a panel to stop it splitting - and both are equally the ordinary English words for a child in another person's care and the bed an infant is kept in, so the fascia indexes the chapter twice without printing a word of it and without the cinema mis-cue that PALACE carried. The isomorphism is the real basis: the conservator dates damage by how far it has aged, which is bruise dating; separates inherent vice from inflicted damage, which is the whole differential of brittle supports and factory blemishes against a blow; x-rays for what the surface hides, which is the skeletal survey; takes the owner's account without leading her and writes it verbatim because a led account contaminates the record; and files a dated, signed condition report whether or not anyone asked for one, which is the reporting duty. Neglect - half the chapter title and the commonest form - is this trade's own second category and has its own furniture here: the flat dead line running across whole months of the thermohygrograph chart, the tide-mark of damp up a stretcher with bloom clouding the varnish, and the far bay of racks holding works nobody has come back for, their tickets dated years ago.

accepted.pun_explanation: SOMA is the ordinary word for the body and an exchange is genuinely what this building is called and what goes on its name plate, so the pun sits on real signage rather than an invented business and the fascia never says somatic. The trade then hands the chapter its central finding as a rubber stamp it already owns - NO FAULT FOUND - and the frame is an entire nervous system in one inanimate object, every jumper on it intact end to end while the reported fault is completely real to the caller and completely absent on the meter, which is functional neurological disorder as a physical fact rather than a metaphor. accepted.pun_explanation: -azine is buried inside SIMAZINE, an ordinary herbicide that a farm-chemicals counter really does sell by the sack and really does paint on its board beside ATRAZINE, so the class hook is carried the way GAZING carried it - inside a real word on real signage - instead of being printed bare as the chemical term, and the trade is not a colour-matching one, so it does not sit on top of the dye house or the conservation studio. The counter owns the chapter's hardest fact outright: the application-rate chart runs from twenty grams a hectare at the top to five kilos a hectare at the bottom, which is the chlorpromazine-equivalent table in the merchant's own units, and one sack alone carries a red MAXIMUM RATE - DO NOT EXCEED band, the ceiling that exists for the heart rather than for the effect. Photosensitivity and slate-blue skin come off the shelves without invention - sample sacks bleached pale down the sun side of the window, and the tub of Bordeaux mixture with blue-grey handprints round its rim and up the shelf edge - the brown-lensed spray goggles on the PPE hook carry the retinal pigmentation, the old hessian sacks of the pre-war lines still stood at the far end beside the new plastic drums carry 'first generation' with no digit anywhere, and the whole yard stands in full sun.

accepted.place: A working cooperage on an ordinary morning: the test bay down the middle with a filling stand-pipe over a floor grating, casks standing on end along both walls with their gallonage stencilled on the head, and the raising fire and hoop-driving block at the far end. The men's snap bench and stove are in the corner by the window, and a shaving horse and a rack of staves fill the wall behind them.
accepted.activity: Everyone is testing a cask — rolling it onto the stand, filling it to the bunghole from the hose, tapping it round with the sounding hammer to hear where it is, then drawing the bung and letting the whole lot go straight down the grating.

accepted.pun_explanation: BULLIMORE is a real family name that carries B-U-L-I-M as an ordered subsequence in the expreSS tRIps manner and reads out loud as BULL-MORE, which is exactly what the word means — Greek bous limos, ox-hunger — so the fascia is the term's own etymology painted as a family firm and no clinical word appears on it. The trade is then the cycle itself: a cask is filled to the bung in one go and emptied down the grating in minutes, over and over, several times a week, and the register on the bench is ruled a line a week with the last twelve weeks ticked; and because a cask looks precisely the same full or empty from outside, this trade tests it by tapping it, which is why bulimia at an unremarkable weight is invisible unless you ask. The medical mimics are the cooperage's ordinary defects and are already chalked on the stock: staves eaten thin and pale on the inside where the liquid stood and the chime worn back (dental erosion), the pair of casks at the door swollen at the bilge with EASE HOOPS chalked on them (parotids), one split lengthwise at the head from being filled too hard (Mallory-Weiss), the potash drum run low (potassium), and every man's knuckles skinned by the hoop driver with the plaster tin left open beside it. Shape is what this trade judges everything by — the shape gauge is held to the bilge and a cask off shape is worth nothing however sound it is — and the one cask standing bunged and still full in the corner, chalked LEFT FULL, is the binge that is never got rid of.

The shop was chosen because every object the fixed glyph needs is already its stock: the tarot deck under a rubber band, the crystal ball on a doily, the lava lamp, the dream catcher, the astrological chart and the four layers of donated clothing a rummage puts on a real customer's back, so odd appearance needs no inventing. The criteria hardest to draw are the ones the trade supplies best: the shoebox of second-hand greetings cards is a rack of messages addressed to a stranger in the second person — THIS IS YOUR DAY, SOMEONE IS THINKING OF YOU — and the customer standing with one of them open is idea of reference on pre-printed stock, doubled by the donated television plugged in to prove it works with its presenter apparently talking straight at her. The differential is native too: the foxed mirror and the crackling transistor are unusual perceptual experiences that anyone can check are simply a bad mirror and a bad radio, because nothing here is actually psychotic and everything works once you wind it. Treatment is on the tickets — the hand-written HOW IT WORKS card tied to the mangle, worked through step by step with a customer, is skills training done as shop routine, and the transistor left playing with its volume screwed right down under a ticket reading WORKS — TURN DOWN, NOT OFF, is the low-dose second line. flagged.place: A battery charging and testing works on an ordinary weekday: a long charging bench with cells wired up in a row along it under a switchboard of dials and a lamp bank, a lead-burning bench and stacked lead plates behind, an acid store of carboys in wicker crates by the back door, a strip-down bay at the far end where cells that will not come round are taken out of service, and a counter at the front with the job dockets on a spike.
flagged.activity: Everybody is putting a battery through the shift's routine - lifting one onto the bench, drawing acid into the hydrometer and reading the float, clipping the load tester on and watching the needle drop, topping up from the distilled water jar and chalking the docket.
flagged.anchor_structure: The charging bench and its busbar run - the row of wired-up cells along it with the switchboard of dials and the lamp bank above - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the works into the counter, the charging run, the test bay and the lead bench behind.
flagged.pun_explanation: A cell is literally an object with two poles, stamped + and - at the terminals, and a works full of them is the plain-English picture inside the diagnosis; POLE is one morpheme on an ordinary firm's fascia and nothing else on the sign is asked to carry the rest, because the stamped terminals do it. The trade's own life unit is the cycle, so rapid cycling is not a metaphor here: the counter drum on the test rig reads in cycles and is wound round to 4, and the wall chart gives cell life in cycles too. Mania against hypomania is which job a battery is on - the long bench charge that takes it out of the vehicle and out of service, against the quick boost that leaves it in and running. Duration lands on the chalked days-on-charge card, a carrier whose whole job is counting days, with 7 against one job and 4 against another. Mixed features is one cell on the bench gassing hard at a terminal while its own meter needle sits flat. The strip-down bay is where a cell that cannot be brought round is taken out of service, which is the hospitalisation criterion in the trade's own words. A battery reading high because the alternator is overcharging it is the works' standing warning and is secondary mania. The see-saw is traded for the beam balance deliberately: it is a plank on a central knife-edge between two extremes, and it hangs hard over to one side and stays there the whole shift, which is Bipolar I as a sustained episode rather than a swing.

This record puts the two enamel charge-rate cards on the wall behind the balance, so the plate shows a beam with an identical lead plate in each pan and two unrelated wall signs: nothing says which end is mania and which is depression. Cue collision with ch143 GOLD STANDARD ASSAY, whose anchor is 'a long testing bench with a rack of acid bottles and a row of beam balances'. The iceberg was restored as instructed but only as a printed paper label on one sealed cell - the token has it as a background element, and a thumbnail on a label will not survive the plate.

The rest is the strongest work in the batch and must be preserved intact: the cycle counter drum wound to 4 with cell life quoted in cycles, 7 and 4 chalked on a days-on-charge card, one cell gassing hard at a terminal while its own needle sits flat, the overcharging alternator as secondary mania, and POLE + stamped +/- terminals as a true LITERAL_PICTURE with the diagnosis unprinted.

problems: THE DIAGNOSIS IS PRINTED ON THE SIGN. 'HOARDINGS' is the diagnosis word plus an -S in the largest lettering slot. The defence — that it is the British trade term for a billboard — depends on a reader who holds that Briticism cold. This is a Hebrew-language board course; for its audience 'hoardings' has no ordinary sense competing with the medical one, so the homograph does not fire and the sign reads as the label. Compare the corpus homographs that do work because the ordinary sense is the one everybody has first: TARDY GATE WORKS, SEAM STRESS ALTERATIONS, PARTITION SELF STORAGE. Note also that the record's own predecessor, HOARD'S END SEED BANK, indexed the disorder with a morpheme inside a place-name — the p272 MINIMUM device — and was never faulted for it. ANCHOR IS A VERBATIM REUSE. ch137 ISLAND END PITCHES already anchors on 'the touchline rail with its run of sponsor hoardings, carrying from the lower-left corner of the field up to the changing block at the upper right'. DYS- DOES NOT INDEX, AND DYSART MIS-CUES. The prior round rejected MORPH- because it pointed at chs 83/84. flagged.activity: Everyone is drawing the week's issue - filling the buff form on the sloping ledge, edging a pram forward in the queue, passing a notification slip through the grille, watching a clerk cut the coupons out of the book and stamp it, and carrying the tins away in a shopping bag.
flagged.anchor_structure: The public counter - a run of oak with its brass grille, four numbered hatches and the sloping writing ledge along the queue side - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the room into the waiting benches and prams, the counter itself, the clerks' desks and index drawers, and the open safe and tin store behind.
flagged.pun_explanation: P-P-D stands as an ordered subsequence of letters inside the carved name of an utterly ordinary municipal building - PiPer & DoDD - which is the expreSS tRIps device, and the counter beneath it is the one civic trade whose whole queue is women with newborns drawing an issue in the weeks after delivery, so the chapter's timings, thresholds and rules about what may pass into the milk arrive as the office's ordinary paperwork.

counter tally sheet ruled in sevens with one line in every seven ringed in red

problems: ANCHOR IS THE FOURTH BRASS-GRILLE COUNTER IN THE COURSE. The proposal's anchor is 'The public counter - a run of oak with its brass grille, four numbered hatches and the sloping writing ledge along the queue side - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the room into the waiting benches and prams, the counter itself, the clerks' desks and index drawers, and the open safe and tin store behind.' Compare ch.90 CHASE'S PLEDGE OFFICE: 'The long mahogany pledge counter with its brass grille and the loaded ticket spike standing on it, running from the lower-left corner of the frame to the upper right, splitting the shop into the queue by the open door, the counter...'. Same object class (long wooden public counter, brass grille), same diagonal, same three-zone logic (queue / counter / behind-counter). This is exactly the near-verbatim-anchor charge that killed the previous 112 draft against ch.26.

THE COUNTER-AND-HATCH OFFICE PICTURE IS SATURATED. ch.90 (brass grille counter), ch.143 GOLD STANDARD ASSAY ('brass-grilled trade counter'), ch.66 TARDY GATE WORKS (brass grille, timekeeper's hatch, run of numbered pigeonholes as the anchor), ch.108 MEANS THE CHEMIST (screened dispensing counter, wall of numbered drawers, as the anchor), ch.130 HOTEL LIAISON (reception counter with numbered pigeonhole wall, as the anchor). Five records already anchor on a public counter with a grille or hatch and numbered pigeonholes behind it. The category string 'welfare food office' is clean; the picture is not.

Preeclampsia's primary number carrier is parked off the frame: the record's own place sentence puts the steam gauge 'on the corridor wall by the plant door', and the anchor's zone list does not include the corridor. The red-lined dial is the one carrier for a named chapter aspect and it sits outside the four zones the picture is divided into.

Two of the fourteen stock_props bundle separate objects into one entry - 'sash window wedged open... the ceiling light flickering above it' and 'queue-number display over the hatch and a fire bell in its glass case by the door'. The last pass rejected a prop at ch.114 for exactly this ('bundles an object with a lighting state'), and the flickering light also asserts a second light source against R2.
flagged.fix_hint: Keep everything else - PIPER & DODD as a clean P-P-D subsequence, the trade (a queue that is genuinely all women with newborns), and the number carriers, which are the best in the batch: the tally ruled in sevens, 13 OR OVER - COUNTER 4 for EPDS, CLAIMS WITHIN 42 DAYS / RUNS TO 12 MONTHS, midwives' slips with the third to the tenth clipped together, TWO OFFICERS NEVER ALONE, and the preparations schedule with one line ringed, one struck through and one marked LONG DATED - CLEARS SLOWLY. Also keep the quiet preeclampsia triple already present (swollen sash frame that will not shut = oedema, tin leaking from its seam = proteinuria, red-lined gauge = pressure). Change only the composition: drop the brass grille and the queue/counter/behind-counter split, and anchor instead on a free-standing object no other record owns - e.g. the long sloping-topped island writing desk down the middle of the public hall with the buff forms chained to it and the queue winding round it, hatches closing the end wall behind. Bring the pressure gauge in off the corridor onto a wall inside one of the named zones, and split the two bundled props.

flagged.place: A high-street denim shop mid-afternoon: a double-sided steel rail run down the length of the floor, a three-tier folded stack wall behind it, a fitting-room block of curtained cubicles at the back with the attendant's counter and chalk board at its mouth, and the corner of Temple Street through the window.
flagged.activity: Everyone is trying jeans on - pulling a pair off the rail, having their items counted in at the cubicle mouth and taking a numbered tag, changing behind the curtain, standing at the long mirror, and carrying the rejects back to the counter.
flagged.anchor_structure: The long steel rail run - a double-sided rail hung the length of the shop with the three-tier stack wall ranged behind it - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the shop into the door and window, the rail floor, the fitting-room block and the stockroom door behind.
flagged.pun_explanation: MEN IN JEANS is a perfectly ordinary denim fascia said aloud as MENINGES, so the shop's own stock supplies the chapter's anatomy before a single symbol is added - a stack wall three tiers deep for dura, arachnoid and pia, with the gap between the tiers where everything collects.
stock_props: three-tier folded stack wall, each tier a different denim weight, dropped tags and dust collected in the gap between the second and third tier

attendant's chalk board at the cubicle mouth with columns headed COUNT, TYPE and TAKINGS: cubicle 1 carrying a four-figure count, TYPE written HEAVY DARK and the takings box left blank, cubicle 4 a two-figure count with TYPE written LIGHT
cubicle sign reading 3 ITEMS ONLY with a hook of numbered fitting-room tags beneath it
rail of clear polythene garment covers with one of them gone milky and opaque
garment steamer on a stand, its pressure gauge standing past the red mark
denim jacket on a bust with an unusually stiff upright collar
mannequin laid along the floor with one knee bent that will not straighten
glass tumbler from the staff kitchen pressed flat against a spotted swatch on the counter
aerosol stain remover on the counter lettered APPLY AT ONCE - DO NOT WAIT FOR THE TEST
rail of COLD WASH ONLY stock standing against the window with the TEMPLE ST street sign beyond the glass

thermostat dial on the wall turned hard to its stop, care labels reading 30, 40 and 60 dangling from the pairs hung round it
problems: THE ANCHOR IS CH.105'S ANCHOR. Proposal: 'The long steel rail run - a double-sided rail hung the length of the shop with the three-tier stack wall ranged behind it - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the shop into the door and window, the rail floor, the fitting-room block and the stockroom door behind.' ch.105 PARAPHERNALIA ARMY SURPLUS: 'The long double-sided steel kit rack - a run of shelving and hanging rail loaded to the ceiling - cutting the shop from the lower-left corner to the upper right and dividing the floor into the window bins, the aisle, the fitting cubicles...'. Double-sided rail, same diagonal, same four zones ending in fitting cubicles. ch.105's place sentence also already contains 'four curtained fitting cubicles along the back wall'. Same picture, different trade name.

THE FITTING-CUBICLE SHOP IS TRIPLE-BOOKED. ch.105 (four curtained fitting cubicles, double-sided rack, glass-topped counter, testing bench), ch.49 SEAM STRESS ALTERATIONS (curtained cubicle, three-way fitting mirror, garment rail, numbered claim tickets), ch.115 NEW ROW SHOE FITTERS (fitting bench, wall of stock with the size chalked on every end - the same object as the proposal's stack wall). 'denim shop' is a clean category string sitting on a picture the course has drawn three times.

THE ANCHOR IS NOT THE STRUCTURE THAT CARRIES THE ANATOMY. The whole spatial argument in pun_explanation rests on the three-tier stack wall being dura, arachnoid and pia with the collection gap between tiers - and that wall is demoted to background behind the rail. The largest inanimate thing in the frame should be the thing the chapter's anatomy is drawn on.

ONE PROP RIDES ON PEOPLE AND CARRIES AN UNINTENDED READING. 'door pedestal beeping at the shop's own staff going out, its stop-and-search book open beside it and every entry a young customer' makes a claim about who is in the frame rather than about an object, which is the fault the last pass charged against this batch at ch.128, and as painted it reads to any resident as a retail-profiling gag rather than as immune self-attack.

NO CARRIER FOR HIV, one of the four psychiatric-sequelae targets the last pass named (HSV/temporal lobe, neurosyphilis, HIV, autoimmune). HSV has TEMPLE ST through the glass; neurosyphilis has only the ambiguous 'THE COPIES ARE VERY GOOD' fakes table, which the reduction ticket struck through three times also competes for; HIV has nothing.
flagged.fix_hint: Keep the sign - MEN IN JEANS / MENINGES is the strongest encoding in the batch and it is already the incumbent - and keep the diagnostic props, which genuinely close the gap the last pass named: the COUNT / TYPE / TAKINGS chalk board (cubicle 1 four-figure count, HEAVY DARK, takings box blank vs cubicle 4 two-figure, LIGHT) is the bacterial-vs-viral differential the previous draft had no carrier for; the tumbler pressed flat on the spotted swatch, the stiff collar, the mannequin knee that will not straighten, the steamer gauge past the red mark, the milky polythene cover and APPLY AT ONCE - DO NOT WAIT FOR THE TEST are all correct. Rebuild only the composition so it stops being ch.105: make the three-tier folded stack wall itself the anchor - floor-to-ceiling, running the diagonal, with the sliding library ladder against it and the gap between the second and third tier at eye level - and delete the double-sided rail run and the curtained fitting-cubicle block entirely, moving the chalk board onto the stockroom door frame and the counting onto the counter. Recast the door-pedestal prop as an object-only fact, and find one carrier for HIV out of native denim-shop stock.

flagged.place: The annual family-reunion potluck at a public park's numbered picnic shelter, midday: a long open-sided timber pavilion with a trestle buffet ranged the full length beneath its roof, picnic tables behind it, two gazebos pitched on the grass in front, and cars nosed onto the verge at the kerb.
flagged.activity: Everyone is working the potluck buffet - carrying a covered dish up from the cars, peeling the foil off, spooning food onto a paper plate down the line, writing on the masking-tape label stuck to their own dish, and edging round to sit at their own side's table.
flagged.anchor_structure: The picnic shelter itself - the long open-sided pavilion, its shingled roof and posts running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right with the trestle buffet ranged the full length beneath it - dividing the ground into the grass with the two gazebos, the buffet run under the roof, the picnic tables behind, and the kerb at the top.
flagged.pun_explanation: Public parks letter and number their picnic shelters, so SHELTER 22Q sits on the post as a genuine reserved-pavilion placard while printing the chapter's highest-yield string on ordinary civic signage without naming any syndrome, and the reunion is the venue because its own seating custom - MOM'S SIDE and DAD'S SIDE over two identical tables booked on the same ground - is genomic imprinting drawn as furniture.
stock_props: park permit stapled to the shelter post reading SHELTER 22Q, MAX 25 PERSONS, with the two gazebo permits pinned beside it, both made out for AREA 15
two gazebos on the grass with hand-lettered banners, MOM'S SIDE and DAD'S SIDE, and an identical folding table under each
easel with a hand-drawn family-tree chart, four of the names ruled through and the gaps left blank
chest cooler on the grass with a chain and padlock through its handles and a card taped to the lid: AFTER THE BLESSING
potluck sign-up sheet on a clipboard, dishes numbered down the page, one name written against every line
battered PA horn wired to the shelter post, its diaphragm split so every announcement comes out nasal and breathy
standpipe and hose at the corner of the slab, the collar crimped just above the union so the flow drops away
name-badge table with a marker on a string, the badges already filled in and handed out to strangers at the kerb
open songbook on a music stand with a fiddle case and a guitar case propped under it, the pages thumbed to shreds
rack of children's marionettes set out for the afternoon's turn, their strings tangled together
chalked lane for the three-legged race with wandering footprints tracked across the line
string of party lights along the shelter beam with one section flickering
soap pump, a box of disposable gloves and a card at the head of the buffet: GLOVES BEFORE YOU SERVE
picnic table whose paint has been picked back to bare wood in one patch
problems: THE SIGN PRINTS THE DIAGNOSIS. '22Q' is not a pun on 22q11 deletion syndrome, it is the syndrome's name in the largest lettering slot with a civic alibi in front of it. This is the MAJOR DEPRESSION QUARRY failure exactly: the resident reads the answer off the fascia, and the pun-as-index is spent. The last pass enforced this against ch.114's DE LIRA FARM - a Latin etymology, a strictly weaker offence than the actual locus - so accepting it here contradicts a standing ruling made two records earlier in the same batch.

DERIVATION IS MISLABELLED. ACRONYM_EMBED means the letters sit in order inside ordinary words, as in expreSS tRIps or F. X. TASker. Nothing is embedded here: the string 22Q is printed verbatim with a shelter in front of it. (The record it replaces labelled the same sign LITERAL_PICTURE, which was also wrong. There is no legal derivation for this sign because there is no device.)

THE SIGN INDEXES ONE OF FOUR SYNDROMES. The chapter is Williams, Prader-Willi, Angelman and 22q11 held together by imprinting; the fascia retrieves only the fourth and says nothing about the mechanism that makes them one chapter. The two gazebo banners, not the sign, are doing the chapter's actual indexing work.

ANCHOR ECHOES CH.6. Proposal: 'The picnic shelter itself - the long open-sided pavilion, its shingled roof and posts running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right...'. ch.6 NOR'EAST PINES BANDSTAND: 'The band shell: the shingled timber acoustic hood over the platform, running from the lower left of the frame up to the treeline at the upper right...'. Two shingled open-sided timber park structures as anchors, both splitting the frame into seating and grass. Softer than the ch.105 and ch.90 hits, but it is the same civic-park carpentry.

Residual coverage gaps: 22q11 hypocalcaemia and seizures have no carrier; Angelman's absent speech and the laughter have only the tangled marionettes, since the split PA diaphragm is doing 22q11's hypernasal speech; Williams' hypercalcaemia has nothing.
flagged.fix_hint: The venue is right and should survive - the last pass explicitly said the MOM'S SIDE / DAD'S SIDE gazebo banners were the only thing that ever carried imprinting, and this draft restores them and fixes the rest properly (MAX 25 PERSONS for the psychosis risk, the standpipe collar crimped just above the union for supravalvular stenosis, the padlocked cooler for hyperphagia, badges handed to strangers at the kerb for overfriendliness, gloves at the head of the buffet for thymic aplasia as a present object rather than an absence, the picked-bare picnic table for skin picking; dropping the ice-cream van also clears ch.102). Apply the same remedy this batch already forced on ch.114: move the locus off the fascia and onto a prop. The park permit stapled to the post keeps SHELTER 22Q; the sign_text becomes the reunion's own hand-painted banner across the shelter with an ordinary family surname that carries the mechanism instead of the label - THE DELLS FAMILY REUNION works, since del is the deletion all four share and Dell reads as a plain surname. Then add a hypocalcaemia carrier and one object for Angelman's speech.

flagged.place: A four-storey deck-access block of council flats at midnight: an open concrete stair running up the front from a half-basement bin store to the top deck, turned spindle rails along every balcony, front doors and kitchen windows opening straight onto the decks, a bike rack and meter cupboards at street level, and the lit twenty-four-hour shop in the end unit throwing its neon across the bottom of the stair.
flagged.activity: Everyone is climbing the stair to their own floor and turning in for the night - carrying a bag or a mug up the flights, stopping to lean on the rail at a half-landing, unlocking a door off the deck, pulling a curtain across, putting a light out behind them.
flagged.anchor_structure: The open concrete stair - a zig-zag of flights and half-landings bolted to the front of the block, running from the half-basement drying room up to the top deck - cutting the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the block into the street and shopfront, the first deck, the second and third decks, and the roof line.
flagged.pun_explanation: A deck-access block is a stack of numbered levels reached by one stair, so sleep architecture is the building rather than a metaphor - a descent from the street through the lighter decks to the deep half-basement and back up four or five times a night - and the block's turned spindle rails put the second stage's named waveform on the ordinary name of an ordinary block.
stock_props: caretaker's round card in the entrance hall, clocked at 00:00, 01:30, 03:00 and 04:30
caretaker's noise log on a clipboard, a column headed CALLS PER HOUR with 5, 15 and 30 chalked against three flat numbers

a pair of slippers left in the middle of the second deck and a front door standing open on the latch with no light behind it
a top-deck flat with its furniture shoved back against the walls, a bedside lamp lying on the floor and a folded walking frame by the door
communal vent grille at deck level with two swollen sacks jammed in behind it, the sash below it rattling in its frame

hosts_tokens: CONVENIENCE_STORE_7 - the twenty-four-hour shop occupying the end unit at street level directly under the first deck: its neon fascia lights the bottom of the stair, its clock reads seven, and the night clerk stands at the till behind the glass. It is the only thing in the block still trading, and everyone crossing the frame passes its window on the way to the stair.
problems: DERIVATION STILL MISLABELLED, AND THIS IS THE SECOND PASS. The last pass ruled: 'Derivation is labelled SPATIAL_ISOMORPHISM but the record's own first sentence is a homonym pun on the fascia... Label the device that is actually carrying the sign.' The proposal reordered the sentence and left the field unchanged, and pun_explanation still ends by conceding the point - 'the block's turned spindle rails put the second stage's named waveform on the ordinary name of an ordinary block'. The name encodes the topic through the word SPINDLE; the stair never appears in the name. Corpus precedent for an exact ordinary word sitting inside the topic term is PHONETIC_PUN (ch.69 THE DOWN ESCALATOR, ch.123 ASH LEIGH BATHS).

Minor, and only worth fixing while the file is open: two props bundle separate objects the way the last pass penalised at ch.114 - 'a pair of slippers left in the middle of the second deck and a front door standing open on the latch' and 'milk bottle already put out at the top-deck door and a pram standing in the ground-floor hall'.

Minor: the track pump 'dialled from 5 to 20' repeats the 5/20 pair already carried by the noise log's CALLS PER HOUR 5, 15 and 30 and by the time switch wound round to twenty, on a weak carrier. One of the three should take a different number or go.
flagged.fix_hint: This is a one-field correction - change derivation to PHONETIC_PUN and change nothing else. Do not re-author the record. Everything the last pass asked for is delivered: the token now exists as specified (a lit twenty-four-hour shop in the end unit at street level, neon across the bottom of the stair, clock at seven, night clerk at the till - the same placement ch.5 and ch.79 use), ch.127's spinning-mill twin frame is gone, the parasomnias are all carried by objects rather than by figures (slippers and the open unlit door for sleepwalking, the two pinned notes for night terrors, the top-deck flat with its furniture shoved back against the walls for RBD), and the digit carriers are the best in the batch (caretaker's round at 00:00 / 01:30 / 03:00 / 04:30 for the ninety-minute cycle, CALLS PER HOUR 5, 15 and 30 for the AHI bands, the night-bus timetable with five departures and two ringed early for the MSLT). Note for the dedup ledger: 'deck-access flats' is unique, with a soft conceptual echo to ch.136 THE STAIRCASE LOCKS, which is also numbered levels traversed in order - different picture, worth recording.

flagged.place: A municipal open-air lido on a hot afternoon in the school holidays: a long tiled tank with its depth boards stepping along the wall, guard stands at the corners, a poolside walk of benches, rolled towels and armbands, the changing block and turnstile at the shallow end, and the plant-room door propped open at the far corner. The words are painted in tall letters along the end wall above the diving stage.
flagged.activity: Everyone is swimming the afternoon session - queueing at the turnstile for a wristband, putting their things in a locker, getting in at the shallow steps, working down the tank towards the line of floats, and hauling out at the rail when the whistle goes.
flagged.anchor_structure: The pool tank itself - the long tiled rectangle of water with its depth boards stepping from the shallow steps up to the deep end and the line of floats slung across it - cutting the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the site into the shallow end and its steps, the deep end under the guard stands, the poolside walk with its benches, and the changing block and turnstile behind.
flagged.pun_explanation: THE DEEP END is the plain board painted on every municipal pool and the ordinary English for a crisis, and the tank is the chapter's structure rather than its mood - one graded, numbered depth running from the steps to the deep end, a marked line nobody passes without being banded and checked, and everything sharp taken off them at the gate before they are let in.
stock_props: tiled depth boards along the tank wall stepping 0.9M, 1.2M, 1.8M and 3M
peg strip of red, amber and green wristbands at the kiosk with a card explaining each band
guard stand with a rota clipboard and a chalked line along its rail: 10 SECONDS TO SEE, 20 TO REACH
whistle on a lanyard and a laminated card of blast codes, one, two and three
rescue board on wall brackets with head blocks and three buckled straps, stencilled TWO GUARDS MINIMUM
valuables cage at the turnstile with numbered pigeonholes and a bin of confiscated glass, lighters and belts beside it
enamelled board over the gate: NO GLASS BEYOND THIS POINT
water-test kit and the plant-room log on the shelf inside the door, pH and chlorine ruled in columns for every hour of the day
session board chalked NEXT SESSION 4.00 with a rack of return tickets stamped with tomorrow's date
notice on the changing-block wall: UNDER 8s MUST BE ACCOMPANIED - ONE ADULT TO TWO CHILDREN
yellow telephone box on a poolside post with the lido's own address and number written on the card inside the glass
flag pole at the deep end with a yellow flag flying and a red one furled below it
pool clock with a sweep second hand on the changing-block gable
first-aid hut door standing open with a folded blanket and a foil sheet on the shelf inside
problems: THE SIGN IS MOOD-MATCHED, NOT DERIVED. Rule 1 forbids choosing a setting for being mood-matched, and 'THE DEEP END' encodes nothing from the chapter: it matches the metaphor 'going off the deep end'. Contrast the corpus idiom sign this is modelled on - ch.69 THE DOWN ESCALATOR - where de-escalation contains ESCALATOR whole, a letter-level fact. Nothing of 'paediatric', 'psychiatric' or 'emergency' is in the fascia, and the sign carries no paediatric content at all despite that being the word that distinguishes this chapter from ch.69 and ch.80.

DERIVATION LEANS ON THE SAME METAPHOR IT CLAIMS TO REPLACE. SPATIAL_ISOMORPHISM requires the place's structure to map onto the anatomy or the concept. 'One graded, numbered depth running from the steps to the deep end' maps onto graded risk only by the metaphor deeper-equals-worse; risk assessment has no depth axis. The depth boards are a fine number carrier, but they are not an isomorphism, so both the sign and the derivation rest on one figure of speech.

THE CHAPTER'S DIFFERENTIAL IS LOST WITH NO REPLACEMENT. The incumbent record carried the three drug emergencies on three red-edged cards asking for temperature, pupils and reflexes - the highest-yield discrimination in a paediatric emergency chapter, and one of the five named aspects. The lido offers only the plant-room pH and chlorine log in its place, which carries nothing about NMS, serotonin syndrome or anticholinergic toxicity, and nothing separates organic from psychiatric anywhere in the fourteen props.

CATEGORY ADJACENCY TO CH.123 to be ruled on explicitly, not discovered later: ASH LEIGH BATHS is a municipal bathing establishment on a slow weekday, tiled, with numbered arch plates and attendants, and its pun_explanation stakes a uniqueness claim on being 'the one mundane venue in which every square inch of skin on eighteen people is wet, lit and being gone over by hand'. A municipal open-air lido is the second such venue. The anchor objects genuinely differ (heated marble slab platform vs tiled water tank) and no pool exists anywhere else in the 144, so this is a flag rather than the reject reason - but it is the kind of dilution rule 4 exists to catch.
flagged.fix_hint: Two live paths, and the owner should pick before re-authoring. (A) If the owner rules 'open-air lido' clear of ch.123, keep it: relabel the derivation honestly (the sign is an idiom, so LITERAL_PICTURE at best), stop claiming the depth gradient is an isomorphism, and put the three drug emergencies back as three objects at the first-aid hut door - a wall thermometer, a pupil gauge card and a reflex hammer on the shelf - since that aspect cannot be dropped. (B) If not, keep from this draft only what it genuinely bought over the incumbent, which is real: children are natively in frame on a school-holiday afternoon (the dispatch room has no children in it at all, only voices, which is a fatal defect for a paediatric chapter), means restriction is an object rather than a script (the valuables cage, the bin of confiscated glass, lighters and belts, NO GLASS BEYOND THIS POINT), risk is banded on wristbands, and 10 SECONDS TO SEE, 20 TO REACH and ONE ADULT TO TWO CHILDREN are good digit carriers. Then find a venue that meets both hard requirements the lido misses: children present as the ordinary population, and a name that encodes by letters or by the term's literal picture rather than by a crisis metaphor. Check any candidate against ch.123 baths, ch.8 CRAWL & CRUISE soft play, ch.137 municipal playing fields, ch.134 lakeside camp archery, ch.82 campground and ch.16/17 (karts, amusement arcade) before committing.

flagged.place: A high-street locksmith's on a Tuesday morning: a long counter down one side with two cutting machines bolted along it, a wall board of blanks hung in numbered rows behind, and a glazed workshop at the back. A spare door leaf and frame stand in the corner as a test rig, and the call-out van is at the kerb with its back doors open. The customer side is full, everybody holding one original key.
flagged.activity: Everyone is having a key copied and a lock looked at — handing the original across the counter, watching the blank traced round under the stylus, then trying the fresh cut in the test cylinder clamped to the end of the bench.
flagged.anchor_structure: The counter run: the long bench with the two cutting machines bolted along it and the numbered blank board rising behind, cutting the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the shop into the waiting side, the counter, the machines and the glazed workshop beyond.
flagged.pun_explanation: Said aloud, the proprietor's ordinary signwritten name — LEE AYSON — is liaison, so the largest lettering in the frame is a surname on a fascia and not the chapter's own word. The trade was chosen because a locksmith holds the consultant's exact position: he is called to premises he does not own, he opens what the owner cannot, and the card on the till says he can advise on the door but the door is the owner's to change. The rule every locksmith is taught first, that you check the door and the frame before you condemn the lock, is the C-L rule that the physical cause is ruled out before anything is attributed to psychiatry; the intermittent lock that only sticks late and cold is delirium's fluctuation drawn as an ordinary trade complaint, and the returned lock tagged NO FAULT FOUND — DOOR HAS DROPPED is the functional presentation exactly, a real symptom whose fault is not in the part it is named after. flagged.place: A demolition site on a terraced street at mid-morning: the block behind already down to clean sorted rubble, the original front wall still standing and held upright by a steel frame of raking shores. A long-reach machine picks at the back, hoses damp the dust down, and a fenced pedestrian walkway is kept open straight through the middle of the works.
flagged.activity: Everyone is working the takedown — wetting down, picking the structure apart in the posted order, and sorting what comes off into the right skip.
flagged.anchor_structure: The steel frame of raking shores propping the retained front wall, its diagonal legs running from the lower-left pavement up to the head of the wall at the upper right.
flagged.pun_explanation: D, B and T head the three words of an ordinary contractor's board, and this contractor's job is the dialectic itself made out of steel. Facade retention is routine, licensed, unremarkable temporary works: the front wall is kept exactly as it is, propped and unchanged, while everything behind it is taken down and rebuilt, and it is the only mundane thing that holds acceptance and change true at the same moment. Nothing here is dramatic — it is a calm, wetted-down, heavily documented morning, and the mnemonic is the propped wall, not the rubble. The rest is the site's own paperwork. The posted sequence of works, numbered and worked strictly top down, is the target hierarchy; the orange tag wired to each prop saying it is temporary and must not be removed is tolerating a load you cannot yet fix; the bowser damping down so nothing flares is regulation; the banksman and the driver working one agreed set of hand signals is asking for what you need in a code both sides already have; the dust monitor on its tripod, recording what is actually in the air and doing nothing about it, is observing and describing without acting; and the public footpath fenced straight through the middle of the works, kept open all day between the two halves of the job, is walking the middle path. The four in hi-vis round a drawing on a tailgate before anyone touches anything are the consultation meeting, the twenty-four-hour number on the hoarding is the between-session call, the permit board with its slots and its pen on a string is the diary card, and the rigger walking a lifting chain link by link with a paint stick to mark the one link that let go is a chain analysis drawn exactly.
